Class ChaosQuarkusRecorder

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.quarkus.ChaosQuarkusRecorder
public class ChaosQuarkusRecorder extends Object
Quarkus build-time recorder that installs the chaos agent at runtime initialization.

Recorders are invoked by Quarkus' build-time processor during image build. The generated bytecode calls installAgent() from the generated runtime-init hook, which triggers a self-attach via ChaosPlatform.installLocally() — but only when ENABLED_PROPERTY is set to true on the launched JVM, by a launch-time local source (see chaosEnabled()). When the flag is absent or false the recorder is a no-op, so the extension jar can ship with production artefacts without triggering byte-code instrumentation in every environment. The same property gates the Spring Boot starters and the Micronaut configurer so one configuration switch controls all supported stacks.

The returned RuntimeValue is a boolean marker — its value reflects whether the install call was actually executed (i.e. the gate was open). Consumers that need the live ChaosControlPlane should obtain it via the CDI-managed ChaosArcProducer.

      public ChaosQuarkusRecorder()

  • Method Details

    • installAgent

      public io.quarkus.runtime.RuntimeValue<Boolean> installAgent()
      Installs the chaos agent in the current JVM if ENABLED_PROPERTY resolves to true; otherwise returns immediately without touching the chaos platform. Idempotent when enabled: ChaosPlatform.installLocally() tolerates repeated invocations on a JVM that already has the agent installed.
      Returns:
      a RuntimeValue holding true when installation succeeded and the gate was open; false when the gate was closed or installation threw. Returning a value instead of throwing keeps Quarkus startup resilient when the chaos platform is unavailable — production traffic must not fail to boot because of an optional observability add-on.
